questions.question: Which relationship best summarizes the hemodynamic basis of arterial pressure?
choices: MAP ≈ cardiac output × systemic vascular resistance
MAP ≈ potassium × heart rate
MAP ≈ GFR × respiratory rate
MAP ≈ LDL × body weight
questions.explanation: A useful physiologic approximation is MAP ≈ cardiac output × systemic vascular resistance; antihypertensives alter one or both components.

questions.question: Which monitoring concern is particularly important after initiating a RAAS-active medication?
choices: Potassium and kidney-function trend
Vision testing only
White blood cell count only
Body temperature only
questions.explanation: RAAS-active medications can affect potassium, hemodynamics, and kidney function, so follow-up must be individualized and drug-specific.

questions.question: Why should multiple RAAS blockers not be combined casually?
choices: They always eliminate all blood pressure benefit
They can increase kidney and potassium-related risk without routinely improving the plan
They have no physiologic effect
They are used only for viral illness
questions.explanation: Combination RAAS blockade can increase adverse renal and potassium effects and needs a specific evidence-based indication and close oversight.

questions.question: A patient develops bilateral ankle edema after a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker, without dyspnea or congestion findings. What is an important consideration?
choices: Medication-related arteriolar dilation may be contributing
The patient definitely has heart failure
The patient must have an infection
A diuretic should be added without assessment
questions.explanation: Peripheral edema can occur from arteriolar dilation with this class. Assess the whole clinical picture rather than assuming volume overload.

questions.question: What is the primary hemodynamic purpose of a loop diuretic in a congested heart-failure patient?
choices: Increase intravascular volume
Reduce sodium/water retention and filling pressures
Increase potassium retention in every patient
Treat all forms of hypertension first line
questions.explanation: Loop diuretics promote natriuresis and reduce congestion and filling pressures; overdiuresis can create hypotension, AKI, and electrolyte problems.

questions.question: Which situation most strongly requires emergency evaluation rather than routine outpatient blood-pressure titration?
choices: Stable elevated readings with no symptoms
A request to review home readings
Severe blood pressure with new unilateral weakness and speech difficulty
Mild ankle edema without other symptoms
questions.explanation: New focal neurologic symptoms may indicate acute target-organ injury and require emergency evaluation.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the role of beta blockers in hypertension management?
choices: They are identical to diuretics
They are often especially useful when there is a compelling indication such as selected HF, prior MI, angina, or arrhythmia
They require no heart-rate monitoring
They can always be stopped abruptly
questions.explanation: Beta blockers have important indication-driven roles and require attention to heart rate, conduction, adverse effects, and safe medication changes.

questions.question: Before labeling hypertension as resistant, what should be reassessed?
choices: Only the patient’s age
Measurement technique, adherence, interacting substances, white-coat effect, volume status, and secondary contributors
Only the medication brand
Whether the patient prefers a different clinic
questions.explanation: Apparent resistance may reflect inaccurate measurement, nonadherence, substances, volume excess, or secondary causes rather than failure of all treatment.

questions.question: Why is pregnancy potential relevant when considering RAAS-active medication?
choices: It never affects medication safety
These drugs have important pregnancy-related safety considerations requiring current reference checking and planning
It matters only after a prescription is dispensed
It replaces kidney-function assessment
questions.explanation: Medication safety includes pregnancy planning and use of current drug-specific guidance for patients who could become pregnant.

questions.question: Which follow-up plan best reflects FNP-level antihypertensive management?
choices: Change a medication without discussing monitoring
Specify home readings, symptoms, relevant labs, adverse-effect guidance, and reassessment timing
Wait indefinitely for symptoms to resolve
Treat a single office reading as the complete diagnosis
questions.explanation: Safe chronic hypertension care uses longitudinal readings, patient-specific monitoring, laboratory follow-up when indicated, and clear safety-net instructions.
